flashcard_questions.q: What is tension in a material?
flashcard_questions.a: A pulling force that stretches the material along its length.

flashcard_questions.q: Which force squashes or shortens a material?
Which two forces combine when a material bends?

flashcard_questions.a: A twisting force that causes rotation along a material's axis.

flashcard_questions.q: Which force do scissors apply to paper?
Which material is strong in compression and used for building foundations?
Why do the top and bottom of a loaded plank behave differently?
flashcard_questions.a: The top is compressed while the bottom is in tension.

flashcard_questions.q: Which cross-section resists torsion most efficiently?
What is lamination as a reinforcement method?
flashcard_questions.a: Gluing thin layers of material together to increase strength.

flashcard_questions.q: Why does plywood resist warping and cracking?
flashcard_questions.a: Its veneers are glued with alternating grain direction.
A triangular plate used to reinforce a joint and resist bending.

flashcard_questions.q: How does folding a flat metal sheet make it stiffer?
flashcard_questions.a: The fold creates a flange or box section that resists bending.

flashcard_questions.q: Which reinforcement is ironed onto collars and cuffs to add structure?
Which structural shape turns a downward load into compression along its curve?
Why is a triangulated frame efficient at spreading loads?
flashcard_questions.a: A triangle cannot deform without changing the length of a side.
